items.title: Read the actual gh tracking metadata and valid YAML
items.today: FrontMatterParser recognizes top-level fields and skips indented mapping entries. Current gh writes tracking data under metadata.github-*. A fixture containing repository, ref, tree SHA, source path and a pinned ref produced null provenance/hash and Pinned=false. A folded description became the literal >-, and scalar allowed-tools was lost. Merely finding frontmatter fences does not validate required fields.
items.change: Use a bounded YAML parser compatible with Native AOT, or a thoroughly tested parser that handles mappings, block scalars and quoted values. Model repository, source subpath, resolved ref, tree SHA, exact pinned ref, local-path, authored version and compatibility separately. Keep legacy readers for old installs. Produce distinct parse, format, compatibility and integrity diagnostics; missing description/name must not look healthy. Preserve unknown agent extensions rather than rewriting them.
items.acceptance: Round-trip-read fixtures created by actual gh remote, pinned and --from-local installs; folded/literal descriptions; string allowed-tools; nested metadata.version; invalid/missing required fields. Verify source links and pin badges against gh list. No silent YAML alias expansion or unlimited reads.

items.title: Merge physical installs once while preserving all observations
items.today: LocalInventoryService.Merge marks a filesystem match Both but discards the matching gh record’s source, version, pin and hosts. Repeating a gh record for one path creates two InstalledSkill rows; a probe then generated a Duplicate candidate for that same physical path. InstalledSkill also stores only one Scope and ScanRoot even when several discovery paths share a target.
items.change: Accumulate observations in a canonical-path index before emitting rows. Merge gh agent hosts and tracking metadata with filesystem link/validity information, recording disagreements instead of choosing silently. Preserve each discovery path, agent, scope and context. Normalize agent identifiers through a catalog: claude versus claude-code, gemini versus gemini-cli, and copilot/github versus github-copilot are currently different strings. A shared .agents location is a discovery convention, not itself an AI agent.
items.acceptance: One physical row for direct, symlink and ancestor aliases; multiple exposures survive. Conflicting metadata remains visible. Same target exposed in project and user contexts preserves both. Scope/agent filters produce the expected installs without generating artificial duplicates.

items.title: Replace name-only duplicate cleanup with evidence-based comparisons
items.today: CleanupClassifier groups by case-insensitive Name and chooses a preferred row by provenance, creation time and shortest path. It does not compare contents, source identity, revision, scope, local changes or agent compatibility. A fixture with intentionally different user/project versions became a Duplicate candidate. On this Mac, 13 same-name groups all had different bounded file-tree hashes, yet generated 39 Duplicate candidates. Those are candidates, not evidence of 39 safe deletions.
items.change: Classify same-name/different-origin, same-origin/different-revision, customized fork, intentional context override, byte-identical copy, and aliases of one target separately. Use source identity and whole-payload fingerprints, with a separately documented normalization for recognized installer metadata. Show differing scripts/references as well as SKILL.md. Suggest a survivor only after checking consumers, pins and modifications; never prefer an older copy because its creation time is earlier.
items.acceptance: Different origins, pins, versions and project overrides never enter bulk safe cleanup. Identical copies require an exposure-preserving migration plan. Different paths to one object count as aliases. Compare all files, not only the markdown body. Case-sensitive naming behavior follows each agent.

items.title: Distinguish incomplete inventory from genuine orphaning
items.today: CaptureAsync sets UsedGhSkillList=true whenever a gh path was supplied. The list adapter returns an empty record array on command/schema failure, so capture cannot distinguish failure from a valid empty catalog. SourceOrphaned is also assigned when a filesystem skill is absent from the default gh scan, although custom roots and agent-only paths can legitimately be outside that scan.
items.change: Return provider status, covered roots, diagnostics and freshness with inventory records. Reconcile absence only within successfully observed coverage. Add gh list --dir calls for custom roots and appropriate explicit agent/scope queries. Label unknown owner, untracked, unsupported discovery location, inaccessible and incomplete scan separately. Reserve orphan/cache-garbage conclusions for verified owner records and known references; lack of GitHub metadata is not proof of disuse.
items.acceptance: A gh failure, invalid JSON, inaccessible root or uncovered custom root generates a diagnostic and no removal recommendation based on absence. A valid [] result remains distinguishable. Credentials/network failures do not become deleted-upstream diagnoses.

items.title: Make selected updates work in the captured subprocess
items.today: The u/U paths pass skill names but set All=false. ProcessRunner redirects stdin/stdout/stderr, so gh cannot ask for confirmation. An actual gh 2.102.0 fixture with an available update exited 1 with a request to rerun with --all; the fixture remained unchanged. No-op updates can hide this defect.
items.change: Separate target selection from noninteractive apply confirmation. After SkillView has a reviewed plan, invoke gh skill update with explicit names and --all: gh applies its name filter before using --all to suppress prompting. Do not represent the confirmation switch internally as “select every installation.” Pass an option terminator before positional names, validate selectors, and keep dry-run distinct from apply.
items.acceptance: A real available update succeeds for a selected fixture, with unrelated fixture names untouched. Test u, U, Update and CLI paths, not merely the generated args or a stubbed successful runner. Verify that all-mode cannot silently expand a marked selection.

items.title: Update an exact installation rather than every matching name
items.today: The UI converts selected physical rows to Name values. gh name filtering scans all its supported project/user roots, so one name can identify several copies. The update adapter does not expose --dir, although gh supports it. A custom root included in SkillView’s pre/post inventories is therefore not included automatically in the gh update scan. Simply adding --all to fix M05 would make this ambiguity actionable.
items.change: Carry installation ID, exact discovery path, physical target, source subpath and context through the plan. Group gh updates by a verified containing skills directory using --dir, preserving namespaced selectors. Detect every same-name target gh would affect and every agent sharing the selected target. If gh cannot express the intended selection, refuse that plan or fetch the exact source to staging using gh install and apply a controlled repair. Do not claim --agent/--scope filters exist on gh update.
items.acceptance: Two copies of one name in different agents/scopes: selecting one changes only its intended target, except explicitly shown shared consumers. Custom and namespaced roots update correctly. Never treat the target skill directory itself as the --dir skills root. Add CLI --path/--install-id selectors and reject unsupported flags.

items.title: Preserve both output streams and verify partial outcomes
items.today: The parser recognizes arrows/colon statuses, but current gh prints hash transitions with > and completion lines beginning Updated. The captured fixture output produced zero parsed entries. Pin, metadata and repository notices often arrive on stderr, which normal result rendering omits. On this machine, a real SkillView --all --dry-run --json returned succeeded=true with empty entries/added/changed and no raw output streams; the direct gh dry-run reported metadata-less skips. UpdateResult.Failure drops stdout; failed apply returns before the CLI rescan, and the TUI requests an inventory refresh only on success.
items.change: Retain both streams on every outcome and classify notices separately from faults. Parse known real formats by supported gh version; unknown lines remain visible rather than disappearing. Describe update available separately from updated. Rescan/invalidate after every attempted mutation, including partial failure and cancellation, and compute per-target outcomes from contents, references and metadata. Exit 0 with skips is not “everything updated”; zero parsed rows is not “no updates.”
items.acceptance: Fixtures for updated, pinned, untracked, remote failure, force reinstall, no-op, partial failure and cancellation. First target succeeds/second fails: preserve stdout and report the first change. Force restoration with unchanged tree SHA still appears as a real file change.

items.title: Protect local changes before update or force repair
items.today: There is no local payload-versus-upstream drift comparison or persistent undo history. gh uses recorded upstream tree metadata for availability, not SkillView’s current file fingerprint. In a disposable fixture, gh 2.102.0 --all --force removed an extra local file and .skillview-ignore. This contradicts its help text promising extra files remain. gh’s temporary backup during content replacement is not a user-accessible durable rollback.
items.change: Stage the approved source revision via gh, compare the complete payload against both the installed files and the recorded base, and offer preserve/merge, fork, replace-with-backup or cancel. Distinguish restore this revision from move to latest and unpin. Snapshot custom files, permissions and links outside the managed directory before mutation; keep a restore journal. Store ignore/suppression preferences outside skill payloads. Use version-specific behavior tests instead of relying on flag presence to imply stable semantics.
items.acceptance: Changed tracked file, extra file, deletion, pin, shared symlink target and unchanged upstream tree SHA are all covered. No overwrite without an explicit disposition of local changes. Verified rollback restores extras and exclusions. Preserve the observed doc/runtime disagreement in compatibility tests.

items.title: Read lockfiles in context and preserve manager ownership
items.today: SkillLockFileReader reads .skill-lock.json at scan-root parents and the home .agents fallback, builds one name-to-package map, and uses first-lock-wins. That source is then assigned to every same-name install, potentially across unrelated contexts. Current Vercel project locks use skills-lock.json at the project root; global locks can use XDG_STATE_HOME. A project-lock fixture was missed and two same-name lock entries collapsed to team/A. Tree hash, source subpath and ref fields are not modeled.
items.change: Implement provider/schema-version readers for global/project locks, retaining lock path, covered scope, source, skill subpath, ref, content hash and installation mode. Match an entry to actual installs through paths/content/exposures and retain conflicts when uncertain. Recognize gh tracking and local-source metadata separately. Publish package/owner information in CLI JSON as well as TUI details. For manager-owned mutations, use its supported operation or a coordinated migration; plain deletion must not silently leave ownership records inconsistent.
items.acceptance: Same skill name in user and two projects with three different sources stays separate. Test current global/project/XDG locations and old schema fixtures. Package/repository group removal never includes an unrelated copy because of a name collision. Unknown schema versions remain read-only diagnostics.

items.title: Discover namespace containers, agent roots and contexts correctly
items.today: Filesystem scanning visits immediate children only. A valid author/demo/SKILL.md fixture was represented as a malformed author directory. Local seeds cover three project and eight user conventions; gh recognizes substantially more agents. Only the git root’s project seeds are considered, not intermediate working-directory scopes. Plugin cache roots and hidden bundled-system roots are not default inventory sources.
items.change: Treat namespace/package containers separately from skill roots. Share one agent capability catalog between installation, scanning and Doctor, including verified config overrides and custom paths. Enumerate bounded recognized structures with cancellation, no arbitrary home-directory crawl. Add explicit workspace collections and per-agent ancestor discovery policies. Show excluded, inaccessible and unsupported locations. Managed/built-in resources are observable but protected; discovery must not grant removal authority.
items.acceptance: Namespaced gh installs, monorepo ancestors, alternate profiles, custom paths and shared roots appear with correct ownership and context. Containers are not offered as malformed skills. Scan budgets report partial coverage and never manufacture orphan conclusions when hit.

items.title: Model identity, revisions, physical installs and agent exposures separately
items.today: InstalledSkill is primarily a path with one name/scope and memberships. It cannot fully represent one source at several revisions, one physical directory used in multiple contexts, or one skill delivered by both a native plugin and a loose copy.
items.change: Introduce four explicit layers: source identity (provider + normalized repository/package/local origin + source subpath); revision (authored version, resolved ref, commit/tree SHA, local payload fingerprint); physical installation (path/object identity, materialization mode, owner record); and exposure (agent/profile/version, discovery path, scope/context, enabled state and loading rule). An installation can have many exposures; one logical skill can have many intentional revisions. Unknown source is an explicit state, never a name-derived identity.
items.acceptance: Represent a shared user install, a pinned project copy, a locally edited fork and a plugin-bundled copy of the same display name without losing information. Every update/delete operation resolves to physical IDs and enumerates affected exposures.

items.title: Explain what each agent can actually load
items.today: Filesystem existence and gh catalog membership do not establish runtime availability. Health badges prioritize Symlink even for a broken symlink. No inventory state explains disabled, shadowed, namespaced, policy-restricted or incompatible skills.
items.change: Build an effective-skills view for a selected agent/profile/project. Agent-specific rules matter: current Claude documentation gives enterprise, personal and project priority in that order for certain same-name commands, while plugin skills are namespaced; Gemini uses workspace over user and favors .agents within a tier; Codex says equal names can both appear. Keep these rules versioned and cited. Separate observed runtime state from filesystem-derived expectation; query native inventories where available without launching skill code.
items.acceptance: Explain why a skill is unavailable and which copy is selected or which names coexist. Disabled, broken and incompatible states outrank a generic symlink badge. Do not apply the generic client guide’s project-over-user advice as a universal rule for every agent.

items.title: Offer repairs matched to the diagnosis
items.today: Cleanup primarily offers removal, ignore and export. Installed removal additionally supports agent unlinking and package/repository groups. Doctor checks the host environment. There is no unified repair plan for drift, fragmented copies, lost provenance or damaged links.
items.change: Create explicit actions: compare copies; restore exact known revision; update a chosen installation; reinstall missing payload files from a verified source; relink a broken exposure to a verified existing target; detach a consumer into a private copy; adopt an unmanaged copy; keep an intentional fork; disable for one agent/context; migrate manager ownership; quarantine an obsolete copy; and undo. Present evidence, exact paths, source/revision, affected agents, preserved changes and expected outcome for each action.
items.acceptance: A broken link offers a target-backed repair before unlinking. Missing source does not prompt automatic guessed metadata. A direct-copy-only agent gets a copy rather than a symlink. Repeating an already completed repair is a verified no-op.

items.title: Consolidate fragmented copies without erasing intentional differences
items.today: Current duplicate cleanup picks a preferred directory and proposes deleting others. It does not reconcile different payloads or redirect consumers to a chosen revision.
items.change: Compare complete trees and provenance, select a desired revision per consumer group, stage it through gh when applicable, and optionally use a canonical .agents copy plus links for agents that support that layout. Preserve private/pinned/customized copies for incompatible contexts. Verify new exposures before quarantining old copies. If a consumer supports shared .agents discovery directly, avoid adding another discovery path unnecessarily. Update owner records or deliberately migrate ownership after verification.
items.acceptance: Four old installs become a demonstrably correct topology with no broken consumer. One project remains pinned while other agents share a newer revision. Different authors using one name are kept distinct. No automatic cross-agent replacement of platform-specific instructions, resources or invocation policy.

items.title: Add plan, stage, verify and recover around the existing safe filesystem backend
items.today: Removal already has strong native identity/containment validation, symlink-leaf traversal, explicit confirmation for warnings, cancellation and progress. That protects destructive boundaries, but does not make a cleanup diagnosis correct. gh performs content replacement with temporary staging/backup; SkillView has no durable multi-step maintenance journal.
items.change: Build inspect → plan → stage → revalidate → apply → verify → record/rollback. A plan pins source revision, expected local fingerprints, topology, owners and native identities where needed. Serialize operations that overlap physical targets; reject changed plans. Keep backups and restartable journals outside skill roots. Retain current secure-removal primitives for quarantine/delete boundaries rather than reintroducing path-recursive deletion. Define cancellation and partial success explicitly; do not promise a globally atomic multi-agent transaction.
items.acceptance: Disk full, interrupted process, canceled worker, target replacement, concurrent native manager update and restart halfway through relinking all leave either a recoverable journal or a verified refusal. Shared consumers are never switched before the chosen payload validates.

items.title: Respect native plugin and extension lifecycles
items.today: Loose skill scans do not cover the complete plugin installation model. Treating a cache version as an ordinary directory loses enablement, dependencies, package integrity and active-version information.
items.change: Keep gh as the install/update provider for supported standalone skills. Add read adapters for native plugin/extension manifests and installation registries. Route native package update/disable/uninstall/prune through its owning manager; use filesystem analysis to find inconsistent exposures or leftover versions. Never flatten a plugin’s skills into loose copies by default: hooks, servers and resources can belong to the package. Codex managed/cloud state may be outside this filesystem; report that boundary. A cache directory is not garbage merely because it is not the latest.
items.acceptance: A plugin skill and a loose same-name skill stay distinct; active/referenced cache versions and persistent package data are protected. Disabled packages remain installed. Owner-driven updates preserve dependencies and mark unresolved capabilities instead of guessing command support.

items.title: Separate latest, pinned, approved and intentionally customized revisions
items.today: The update workflow exposes force and unpin checkboxes; it lacks a durable per-install desired-state policy. A gh ref is not necessarily a skill’s authored semantic version, and an intentional old version is not automatically unhealthy.
items.change: Support follow-gh-default, follow-a-chosen-track where supported, approved immutable revision, exact pin, manual fork and native-manager policies. Show the resolved source and ref before applying: gh normally selects a latest tagged release and otherwise the default branch. Use gh --pin for supported tag/commit installs; do not invent branch-update support that gh does not provide. Record lock/desired state separately from runtime metadata. Export reproducible project skill sets and machine profiles with installation-specific exceptions.
items.acceptance: Routine maintenance leaves pins and forks alone. Unpin is an explicit change for selected installs. Reprovisioning produces the same approved payloads and exposure topology. A branch-only file change can count even when an authored version string is unchanged.

items.title: Recover provenance using evidence instead of guessing from names
items.today: Skills installed manually, from local repos, by Vercel tooling or as plugins may lack gh metadata. gh noninteractive update skips these. SkillView can display some lock source information but cannot review a proposed adoption/migration.
items.change: Use owner records, known local source paths, repository remotes, source subpaths and payload matches to propose provenance with confidence. For uncertain matches, ask the user to choose a source and show a diff. Adopt via a deliberate gh reinstallation to staging plus local-change handling, or retain original ownership and simply record evidence. Preserve the distinction between original upstream author, republishing repository, package distributor and local fork. Make --upstream an explicit source switch.
items.acceptance: Two repositories with the same skill name never produce an automatic adoption. A verified local-path install offers reimport from that source. A disappeared/private remote retains the local payload and reports access/source uncertainty. Metadata is never fabricated solely to make the update button work.

items.title: Review the whole skill package and distinguish quality from safety
items.today: SkillView previews markdown and protects panes from terminal escapes. That does not inspect executable resources, missing referenced files, compatibility requirements or changes to invocation/tool policies. Current healthy state is narrower than these checks.
items.change: Add bounded static lint for required metadata, missing scripts/assets/references, case mismatches, broken internal links, portability and agent-specific configuration. Show content diffs for instructions, scripts and permission/tool declarations before update. Surface newly introduced network destinations or dependencies as review evidence, without declaring a skill safe based on a heuristic score. Offer opt-in isolated evaluations with representative prompts; never execute skill scripts as part of routine inventory. Reuse gh publish --dry-run for authoring validation where its repository discovery fits. gh publish --fix strips installation metadata: it is not a repair command for installed updates.
items.acceptance: Valid format, agent-compatible, intact payload and reviewed source are separate states. Missing dependencies have concrete repair guidance. Evaluations require an explicit runnable environment and cannot silently incur agent/API execution. Preserve user-authored instructions unless a reviewed edit is selected.

items.title: Make the maintenance queue actionable and explain application state
items.today: Changes currently queues cleanup items; update availability stays unknown until a separate dry-run. The Updates table shows name/scope/flags, lacks target/source comparisons, and applies updates without a content-diff plan. Doctor is mostly environment/auth/agent-folder reporting. remove CLI can narrow only by agent when names collide.
items.change: Offer one maintenance queue grouped by issue and physical install, with source, revision, owner, exposures, confidence and recommended action. Permit row→compare→plan→apply→verify. Mark unknown update state honestly and provide an explicit refresh. Add CLI inspect/check/plan/apply/repair/undo with exact IDs, versioned JSON schemas, meaningful skipped/partial/refused codes and a plan-file contract. Separate cleanup suppression, disablement, pinning and migration. Report disk-updated versus active-session state, and agent-specific reload/restart instructions.
items.acceptance: A selected row always identifies exact affected paths. Every skip/partial result explains what happened. Current Claude plugin docs say running sessions retain loaded plugin versions after background updates; display that as a reload requirement, not failed filesystem verification. Runtime state is unknown unless observed.

items.title: Test real gh contracts and adversarial multi-agent scenarios
items.today: The targeted existing test run passed 44 tests, while independent probes exposed the preceding gaps. Several existing fixtures assume top-level tracking fields or update output shapes that do not match the installed CLI. Green tests alone do not establish maintenance semantics.
items.change: Maintain opt-in contract tests for the minimum supported gh and current stable gh, capturing actual metadata, both streams, namespaced paths and mutation results. Supplement unit tests with disposable multi-agent topologies and native-manager registry fixtures. Retain existing cancellation, static Terminal.Gui serialization and secure-removal stress coverage. Cache source queries by repository + immutable revision and limit network/filesystem concurrency. Hash payloads lazily with budgets and cancellation; report incomplete comparisons rather than declaring equality.
items.acceptance: Required scenarios: same name/different origins; pinned and unpinned versions; local edits and extras; direct plus shared links; custom roots; failed provider; namespace containers; project/global lock conflicts; partial update; stale plan; concurrent owner mutation; rollback/restart. Routine inventory remains offline unless a check is requested, and never launches skill code.
